# Egap.Documents.Html: guide for coding agents

Egap.Documents.Html is the HTML add-on for Egap.Documents: HTML and XHTML read into the document model, styled through
the CSS cascade (flexbox, grid, positioned boxes, `@page` rules and margin boxes), and written back; HTML to PDF, HTML
stamps and page bands; MHTML web archives; and EPUB 2 and 3 books read and EPUB 3.3 written. Parsing is AngleSharp's and
the cascade Egami.Css's. Scripts never run.

Namespaces: `Egap.Documents` (`HtmlFormat`, `EpubFormat` and their options keep the names they had in Egap.Documents 1.x),
and `Egap.Documents.Pdf` for `PdfConvert`, `PdfStamp.Html` and `PageBand.Html`.

## Egap's vocabulary

Egap has its own names. Use them, not names from other PDF, Word or Excel libraries: there is no `PdfReader`, `PdfWriter`,
`XWPFDocument`, `Range.Text` or `IWorkbook` in Egap.

- `PdfDocument` (namespace `Egap.Pdf`) is a PDF file: `PdfDocument.Open`, `PdfDocument.Create`, `PdfDocument.Merge`, then
  `Pages`, `Metadata`, `Outline`, `Form`, `Attachments`, `Signatures` and `Save`. It is `IDisposable` and keeps its file open
  until disposed.
- `Document` (namespace `Egap.Documents`) is a flow document: one model for DOCX, DOC, RTF, ODT, plain text, PDF, HTML,
  MHTML, EPUB and Markdown. `Document.Load` and `Save` pick the format; `DocumentBuilder` edits at a cursor. It is not
  disposable.
- `Workbook` and `Worksheet` (namespace `Egap.Spreadsheets`) are an Excel workbook and its sheets; `sheet["B2"]` is a
  `Cell`, `sheet.Range("A1:C9")` a `CellRange`, and `CellValue` a cell's value.
- `Presentation` (namespace `Egap.Presentations`) is a PowerPoint file: `Presentation.Load`, `Slides`, `SlideMasters` and
  `Save`; `slide.Shapes` holds its `SlideShape`s.
- Each format has its own class (`DocxFormat`, `RtfFormat`, `OdtFormat`, `TextFormat`, `HtmlFormat`, `EpubFormat`,
  `MarkdownFormat`) and members on `Document` that forward to it: `Document.LoadDocx`, `SaveAsDocx`, `ToHtml`,
  `SaveAsMarkdown`. `SaveAsPdf` and `PdfConvert` (namespace `Egap.Documents.Pdf`) write PDF.
- Options are objects with `init` properties, set in an object initializer and passed to the call: `PdfReadOptions`,
  `PdfSaveOptions`, `PdfRenderOptions`, `PdfExportOptions`, `PdfConvertOptions`, `LayoutOptions`, `WorkbookLoadOptions`.
- Damaged input is repaired and reported, not thrown: `pdf.Warnings` (`PdfWarning`), a `Load` overload with
  `out IReadOnlyList<ConversionWarning>`, and the list `Document.Save` returns. A `Strict` option throws instead.
- Sizes are PDF points (1/72 inch). `Length.Mm(15)`, `Length.Cm`, `Length.In` and `Length.Pt` (namespace `Egap.Pdf`) turn
  into points by themselves. Page indexes in code count from 0; `PdfPageRange.Parse("1-3,z")` takes page numbers from 1.
- Images, fonts and drawing come from Egami: a page renders to an Egami `Raster<Rgba8>` (namespaces `Egami` and
  `Egami.Pixels`), and draws onto any Egami.Drawing `Canvas`.
- Egap never opens a network connection by itself: the resolver, base folder or `HttpClient` you pass decides what a
  document may fetch.

## Entry points

- `HtmlFormat.Register()` once at startup: `Document.Load`, `Document.Save` and `PdfConvert.FromFile` then handle `.html`,
  `.htm`, `.xhtml`, `.mht`, `.mhtml` and `.epub`. Calling the format classes directly needs no registration.
- `Document.LoadHtml(path)`, `Document.ParseHtml(html)` and `HtmlFormat.Load(path, HtmlLoadOptions)`: HTML to a document.
- `doc.ToHtml()`, `doc.SaveAsHtml(path)` and `HtmlFormat.Save(doc, path, HtmlSaveOptions)`: a document as HTML
  (`EmbedImages`, `ImageWriter`, `WritePageSetup`, `RevisionView`).
- `PdfConvert.FromHtml(html, outputPath, PdfConvertOptions)`: HTML text to PDF, with `PageSize`, `Margins`, `Header`,
  `Footer` (`PageBand.Html`, `PageBand.Text`), `TableOfContents` and `Conformance`.
- `HtmlFormat.LoadMhtml(path)` and `doc.SaveAsMhtml(path)`: web archives.
- `Document.LoadEpub(path)`, `EpubFormat.Load`, and `doc.SaveAsEpub(path, EpubSaveOptions)`: e-books.
- `PdfStamp.Html(html, width)`: a piece of HTML laid out as a stamp on PDF pages.
- `HtmlLoadOptions`: `BaseUri`, `ResourceResolver`, `Encoding`, `Media` (`"print"` or `"screen"`), `UserStyleSheets`,
  `Kashida` and `Limits`.

## Samples

HTML in and out, and HTML to PDF:

```csharp
using Egap.Documents;
using Egap.Documents.Pdf;

HtmlFormat.Register();                                           // once at startup: Document.Load and Save know .html
Document page = Document.LoadHtml("invoice.html");
page.SaveAsDocx("invoice.docx");
string html = Document.LoadDocx("report.docx").ToHtml();
PdfConvert.FromHtml("<h1>Invoice</h1><p>Total: 120 EUR</p>", "invoice.pdf");
```

Let a page load its images and style sheets:

```csharp
using Egap.Documents;

Document page = HtmlFormat.Load("invoice.html", new HtmlLoadOptions
{
    BaseUri = new Uri("https://example.com/"),
    ResourceResolver = uri => File.Exists(uri.LocalPath) ? File.ReadAllBytes(uri.LocalPath) : null,
});
```

E-books:

```csharp
using Egap.Documents;
using Egap.Documents.Pdf;

Document book = Document.LoadEpub("novel.epub");
book.SaveAsPdf("novel.pdf");
Document.LoadDocx("handbook.docx").SaveAsEpub("handbook.epub");
```

Web archives:

```csharp
using Egap.Documents;

Document page = HtmlFormat.LoadMhtml("saved-page.mhtml");
page.SaveAsDocx("saved-page.docx");
Document.LoadDocx("report.docx").SaveAsMhtml("report.mhtml");
```

An HTML invoice as a Factur-X PDF/A-3:

```csharp
using Egap.Documents;
using Egap.Documents.Pdf;
using Egap.Pdf;

HtmlFormat.Register();                                           // once at startup: PdfConvert.FromFile reads .html
using PdfDocument invoice = PdfConvert.FromFile("invoice.html", new PdfConvertOptions
{
    PageSize = PdfPageSize.A4,
    Margins = PageMargins.All(Length.Mm(15)),
});
PdfAReport report = PdfInvoice.Embed(invoice, File.ReadAllBytes("factur-x.xml"));   // PDF/A-3b with the XML attached
if (report.Succeeded)
{
    invoice.Save("invoice-2026-118.pdf");
}
```

## Common mistakes

- `Document.Load("page.html")` before `HtmlFormat.Register()`: it throws a `NotSupportedException` naming this package.
  Register once at startup, or call `HtmlFormat` and the `Document.LoadHtml` members directly.
- Expecting images, fonts and style sheets from the web. Nothing outside the page is fetched unless `ResourceResolver`
  returns it; `data:` URLs always work. `PdfConvert.FromFile` reads from the file's own folder (or
  `PdfConvertOptions.BaseDirectory`), never from the network. Keep it that way for HTML from users.
- HTML given as text has no folder: relative images load only from `BaseDirectory` (or `BaseUri` with a resolver).
- Expecting screen styles. Style sheets apply for print media by default; set `Media = "screen"` for the screen rules.
- Expecting JavaScript output. Scripts never run, so content that scripts build is missing; render the page's final HTML
  first.
- Expecting every CSS layout feature: `position: sticky`, subgrid, masonry, named grid lines and inline flex and grid
  boxes are not laid out as such.
- Deep or huge pages: `HtmlLoadOptions.Limits` (`DocumentLimits`) bounds page size and nesting; deeper elements are kept as
  plain text and a page past a limit throws a `DocumentLimitException`.
- Books under DRM are refused when an EPUB is loaded.
